facts.statement: Barnum Brown collected the remains of Nesodactylus in 1918 from rocks known for marine fossils but did not prepare them at that time.
facts.quote: Its remains were collected but not prepared by Barnum Brown in 1918, from rocks better known for their fossils of marine life.

facts.statement: Richard Lund revealed the pterosaur remains in 1966 by preparing seven black chalkstone blocks using acid to dissolve the surrounding rock.
facts.quote: When seven black chalkstone blocks were prepared from 1966 by Richard Lund by dissolving the substrate in acid, this revealed the remains of a pterosaur.

facts.statement: Ned Colbert described and named the genus Nesodactylus in 1969.
facts.quote: Ned Colbert described and named the genus in 1969.

facts.statement: James A. Jensen and John Ostrom mistakenly referred to Nesodactylus as Nesodon in 1977.
facts.quote: In 1977 James A. Jensen and John Ostrom by mistake referred to it as Nesodon (1977).

facts.statement: Nesodactylus lived during the middle-late Oxfordian age of the Upper Jurassic in the Jagua Formation of western Cuba.
facts.quote: Nesodactylus was a genus of rhamphorhynchid pterosaur from the middle-late Oxfordian age Upper Jurassic Jagua Formation of Pinar del Río, western Cuba.

facts.statement: Nesodactylus possessed longer wings, more robust limbs, and longer legs than its relative Rhamphorhynchus, despite being of similar overall size.
facts.quote: Colbert found Nesodactylus to have had longer wings and more robust limbs and longer legs than related Rhamphorhynchus, although of a similar size and overall anatomy.

facts.statement: Nesodactylus is classified as a member of the rhamphorhynchid family.
facts.quote: Nesodactylus is classified as a rhamphorhynchid.

facts.statement: Recent scientific reviews disagree on whether Nesodactylus belongs to the subfamily Rhamphorhynchinae or remains unclassified within that group.
facts.quote: At least one recent review suggests it was a rhamphorhynchine, while another does not classify it.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes a partial skeleton with a skull fragment, vertebrae, a deeply keeled sternum, limbs, and ribs, though bones were not completely removed during preparation.
facts.quote: The genus is based on holotype AMNH 2000, a partial skeleton including a skull fragment, numerous vertebrae from all parts of the spine and tail, zygapophyses (interpreted by Colbert as ossified tendons) on the tail, the pectoral girdle and a very deeply keeled sternum, arms and partial hands, part of the pelvis, parts of both femora, partial metatarsals, and ribs.

facts.statement: Nesodactylus lived between 161.5 and 143.1 million years ago, spanning the Oxfordian to Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Tithonian (161.5 to 143.1 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The genus name is derived from Greek nesos, 'island' and daktylos, 'finger', a reference to the island of Cuba and the typical wing finger of pterosaurs.
